findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: A malicious user could inject a specially crafted command-line argument that causes atoi to misinterpret the input, leading to undefined behavior.
findings.assumptions: The input is not validated before being passed to atoi, and the program does not handle errors from atoi.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: If the user provides a very large value for N, it could cause the shared memory allocation to exceed available system resources, leading to a buffer overflow.
findings.assumptions: The program does not check if the value of N is within a reasonable range before allocating shared memory.

findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: If N is very large, it could lead to excessive process creation, potentially exhausting system resources and leading to a denial of service.
findings.assumptions: The program does not limit the number of processes that can be created based on the value of N.

findings.title: Improper Pointer Initialization
findings.sink: A[i] = shm_A + N*i; B[i] = shm_B + N*i; C[i] = shm_C + N*i;
findings.trigger: If N is very large, it could cause pointer arithmetic to overflow, leading to undefined behavior.
findings.assumptions: The program does not check if the value of N is within a reasonable range before performing pointer arithmetic.
